integrity: The proof identifies every vertex after the cuts, derives a disjoint-orthant lower bound from the surviving cube vertices, and gives an explicit illuminating direction for every new cut vertex using its untruncated neighbor. The metric-nearness estimate is an exact cube sandwich. A standalone exact-rational checker replays the local inequalities and finite families; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The exact count is proved for simultaneous shallow truncations whose selected cube vertices form an independent set. Adjacent truncations are not classified. The one-corner value is prior-known from the direct near-cube source; the claimed new content is the simultaneous independent-set law and the resulting high-half spectrum. Because the proof is elementary, unindexed or folklore prior observation remains a residual originality risk.
title: Independent corner truncations realize the high illumination spectrum near the cube
